newsitem.title: USA: Dataquest says US Cellular market to grow 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dataquest says US Cellular market to grow 30 pct.

text.p: The U.S. cellular market is poised to grow 30 percent in 1996 to 41.8 million subscribers, up from 32.1 million subscribers the previous year, Dataquest Inc said Wednesday.
The research firm said there will be 69.8 million cellular subscribers in the year 2000, and nearly half are expected to be digital subscribers.
Dataquest analysts said the introduction of personal communications services (PCS) networks will drive the change to digital networks.

Dataquest said average monthly revenue per subscriber is expected to reach $59 by the end of the year. Prices will continue to fall as the average monthly revenue per subscriber drops to $45 by 2000, the company said.
Dataquest also said the market for smart phones, which offer e-mail, facsimile and paging, will reach 14,800 units in 1997 and grow to 2.4 million units by the end of 2000.
